## v35 / companion rev 13 audit attempt (rejected, no machine entry)

Claude CLI 2.1.267, model `opus`, effort `high`, and read-only tools read both documents completely but could
not execute `shasum` because the supplied Bash capability was unavailable. It correctly returned `REJECT` with
non-hex digest headers, so the response was intentionally ineligible for the machine fence and the pair remained
blocked. Its substantive read also found the unrecoverable invalid-entry rule and the incomplete global lock-order
claim recorded as R30 in the plan. Version v36 repairs those design defects; this narrative is history, not a verdict
for the current pair.

## v36 / companion rev 13 audit (rejected, no machine entry)

Claude CLI 2.1.267, model `opus`, effort `high`, independently recomputed and matched both digests and read both
documents completely. It returned `REJECT` because plan §8 included the main write lock while companion §4.1
still called a conflicting main-less sequence the program-wide order, companion §7.2 defined a main-write-held
DONE writer, and plan R30 incorrectly claimed companion rev13 was already scoped. The response is documentary
round R31 in the plan and was not appended to the approval fence. Plan v37 and companion rev14 repair that
cross-document conflict; this paragraph grants no current verdict.

## Human-readable result

For the now-superseded v34/rev13 pair, Claude independently recomputed both document hashes, read both files end to end, and returned `VERDICT: APPROVE` with `REQUIRED_CHANGES: - NONE`. It confirmed the query-resolved RED/GREEN scope evidence, characterization path, docs-only exemption, lifecycle gates, concurrent and adversarial evidence selection, performance evidence, migration, component succession, section-8 heading, assurance boundary, enforce-floor design, and R27-R29 repairs were implementation-ready for those bytes. Its non-blocking observations were: the plan's immutable 0.3.296 baseline could coexist with a later local main version provided future implementation Stories refresh live truth; P1 must invert the then-current positive express-exemption assertions in `scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs`; and the v34 text still carried stale v33 self-references. This paragraph records that historical response and does not promote it to the current pair.

For the current v37/rev14 pair, Claude independently recomputed both document hashes, read both files end to end, and returned `VERDICT: APPROVE` with `REQUIRED_CHANGES: - NONE`. It found only non-blocking editorial observations: two summary rows say “descendant” while the normative rule says “strict descendant”; “the tenth member” means the tenth member added although it appears sixth in that local enumeration; and the `scopeContractDigest` explanation references the frozen commit even though the content digest itself is commit-independent and the DEV recheck closes drift. None changes the implementable, fail-closed contract.
